ps: At 9%, every internal reorganisation acquires a tax shadow: moving a property from OpCo to HoldCo, consolidating two licences into one company, hiving a division into its own entity — each is, by default, a disposal at market value with a taxable gain attached. The law provides two pressure valves: qualifying group relief for asset transfers inside a group, and business restructuring relief for mergers and demergers. Both make the move tax-neutral; both come with strings.

Qualifying group relief is Article 26 of the Corporate Tax Law (Federal Decree-Law No. 47 of 2022), with the detail in Ministerial Decision No. 132 of 2023. Business restructuring relief is Article 27, with Ministerial Decision No. 133 of 2023. The FTA has published a guide for each (CTGQGR1 and CTGBRR1), and both are worth reading for their worked examples.

Both reliefs sit in Chapter Eight of the law, which Article 21(2) switches off for a company that elects [Small Business Relief](/guides/uae-small-business-relief). An electing small business cannot use either relief in that period.

sections.h: Qualifying group relief — assets between siblings
list: Available where transferor and transferee are both UAE taxable persons that are juridical persons (resident, or non-resident with a UAE permanent establishment) with 75% common ownership (direct or indirect), neither is an exempt person or a Qualifying Free Zone Person, their financial years end on the same date and both use the same accounting standards

The asset moves at net book value: no gain, no loss, and the consideration is treated as equal to that net book value. The transferee takes the asset at that value for Corporate Tax and makes the adjustments to its accounting depreciation required by the general rules for determining taxable income (Ministerial Decision No. 134 of 2023)

The clawback: if within two years the asset leaves the group, or either party leaves the qualifying group, the relief unwinds — the original transfer is retested at market value as at the transfer date, and the gain is taxed in the transferor's return for the period in which the clawback event happens

ps: Ownership means equity interests under the accounting standards the holder applies, measured against total paid-up capital or total equity contributions (Article 2 of Ministerial Decision No. 132). It can be direct, through a chain, or through a common parent holding 75% of both companies.

The intermediaries do not have to qualify. The FTA's guide says the ownership condition is still met where the 75% runs through an exempt person, a Qualifying Free Zone Person or a foreign company with no UAE presence. In its example, a UAE parent owns 90% of a foreign company that owns 90% of a UAE subsidiary: 81% indirect, so the two UAE companies are in a qualifying group even though the foreign company in the middle is not.

sections.h: Worked example: moving machinery between sister companies
ps: HoldCo owns 100% of OpCo A and OpCo B, both mainland companies with 31 December year-ends and IFRS accounts. On 1 March 2026 OpCo A sells a production line to OpCo B for AED 2,000,000, its market value. Its net book value in OpCo A's accounts is AED 1,300,000. OpCo A elects for qualifying group relief in its 2026 return.
list: OpCo A's books: Dr Intercompany receivable 2,000,000; Dr Accumulated depreciation (as recorded); Cr Plant and machinery cost; giving an accounting gain of AED 700,000 in profit or loss
OpCo A's tax computation: deduct the AED 700,000 gain, because the transfer is treated as made at net book value. Tax saved now: 9% × 700,000 = AED 63,000

OpCo B's books: Dr Plant and machinery 2,000,000; Cr Intercompany payable 2,000,000. Its Corporate Tax base is AED 1,300,000, so it adds back the depreciation on the extra AED 700,000 each year under the general rules for determining taxable income

If OpCo B sells the line to a third party in January 2028, inside two years, the relief unwinds. OpCo A brings the AED 700,000 gain into its 2028 return, and OpCo B reverses the depreciation adjustments it made, so its gain on sale follows its accounts
If the sale happens after 1 March 2028, the relief stands. OpCo B's taxable gain on sale is measured from its AED 1,300,000 tax base, so the AED 700,000 is taxed eventually, in OpCo B, on disposal

sections.h: Business restructuring relief — whole businesses for shares
list: Covers transferring an entire business (or independent part of one) in exchange for shares or ownership interests — mergers, demergers, incorporating a sole establishment into an LLC

The consideration must be substantially shares in the transferee: any other consideration, such as cash, may not exceed the lower of the net book value of the assets and liabilities transferred and 10% of the nominal value of the shares issued (Article 2 of Ministerial Decision No. 133 of 2023). The business must transfer as a going concern, under the applicable UAE legislation, and for valid commercial or other non-fiscal reasons
Same architecture: tax-neutral at transfer, elections apply, and a two-year clawback if the shares are disposed of or the business is on-sold

The parties must be resident (or non-residents with a UAE permanent establishment), neither exempt nor a Qualifying Free Zone Person, with the same financial year-end and the same accounting standards
Unlike qualifying group relief, the restructuring relief has no 75% ownership test at the outset: it can apply between unrelated companies, such as two independent businesses merging for shares

The transferor's unused tax losses can move to the transferee if the transferee carries on the same or a similar business (Article 5 of Ministerial Decision No. 133); see [tax losses](/guides/uae-tax-loss-carry-forward)

The clawback is triggered if, within two years, shares in the transferor or transferee are disposed of to a person outside their qualifying group, or the business transferred is itself transferred or disposed of. The gain at market value on the transfer date goes into the transferor's return for the period of the trigger, or the transferee's where the transferor has ceased to be a taxable person or is a natural person
The election is made by the transferor for each restructuring; it does not carry over to later transactions
Diarise the clawback window per transaction — a sale in month 23 costs what the relief saved, plus the surprise
Paper the ownership maths at transfer date: 75% is tested through the chain, and a later reviewer needs the cap table as it stood

Free-zone complication: the transferor and the transferee must not be Qualifying Free Zone Persons, so sequencing which entity elects which regime is part of the structure. A free zone company that is not a Qualifying Free Zone Person can be a member, and a Qualifying Free Zone Person higher up the chain does not break the 75% test
The reliefs are elective, not automatic — the election is made in the return, and forgetting it converts a tax-neutral reorganisation into a taxable one retroactively

sections.h: The election is wider than one transfer
ps: Ministerial Decision No. 132 of 2023 makes the qualifying group election irrevocable, unless the FTA agrees otherwise on application, and applies it to every transfer of capital-account assets and liabilities the transferor makes to a qualifying group member in that period and later periods. You cannot elect for the property that carries a gain and opt out for the one that carries a loss. Make the first election knowing it sets the policy for the transferor's future intra-group transfers.

The FTA's guide adds that an election made on a transfer that turns out not to meet the conditions is invalid, and the return relying on it is wrong. Check every condition at the transfer date before filing.

list: Using a different financial year-end in one subsidiary: the condition fails and the transfer is taxable at market value
Forgetting the transferee side: OpCo B must keep the lower tax base and its depreciation add-backs for the life of the asset
Selling either company out of the group inside two years: that breaks the qualifying group and triggers the clawback, even though the asset itself never moved again
Missing partial disposals: selling part of the asset outside the group within two years triggers a proportionate clawback (Article 5(4) of Ministerial Decision No. 132)

ps: Hysaab records intra-group transfers with the relief election, the inherited tax base and the clawback date on the asset record, and raises the flag when a disposal or ownership change approaches a live clawback window — the two-year memory that reorganisations depend on and spreadsheets forget.

faqs.q: Can assets move between UAE group companies without Corporate Tax?
faqs.a: Yes, under qualifying group relief: with 75% common ownership and both companies being UAE taxable persons (neither exempt nor a Qualifying Free Zone Person), with the same year-end and accounting standards, assets transfer at net book value with no gain or loss, subject to a two-year clawback.

faqs.q: What is the clawback period for UAE group relief?
faqs.a: Two years. If the asset leaves the group, or either company leaves the qualifying group, within two years of the transfer, the relief unwinds: the transfer is treated as made at market value on the original date, and the gain is included in the transferor's return for the period in which the clawback event happens.

faqs.q: Is a merger taxable under UAE Corporate Tax?
faqs.a: Not necessarily: business restructuring relief makes a merger or demerger tax-neutral where a whole business (or independent part) transfers as a going concern in exchange for shares, with non-share consideration no more than the lower of net book value and 10% of the nominal value of the shares issued, and the transferor elects. There is again a two-year clawback.

faqs.q: Does group relief work with free zone companies?
faqs.a: A Qualifying Free Zone Person cannot be the transferor or transferee under qualifying group relief. A free zone company that is not a Qualifying Free Zone Person can, and a Qualifying Free Zone Person further up the ownership chain does not stop two other companies qualifying.

faqs.q: Is the qualifying group relief election irrevocable?
faqs.a: Yes. Once the transferor elects in its return, the election applies to all its qualifying intra-group transfers of capital assets and liabilities in that period and later ones, and can only be withdrawn with the FTA's approval.

faqs.q: Can a company using Small Business Relief claim group relief?
faqs.a: No. Electing Small Business Relief switches off the reliefs in Chapter Eight of the Corporate Tax Law, which include qualifying group relief and business restructuring relief.
